A monitor for download progress is implemented using the `downloadprogress` event.

results.message: The component's shadow stylesheet sets the host's display with a :host rule
The component's shadow stylesheet does not use :host-context()

Public theming custom properties (such as --card-bg) are read with a var() fallback and are not declared on :host; private aliases on :host that read them (such as --_card-bg: var(--card-bg, white)) are allowed. Setting the public property on any Light DOM ancestor changes the host's or an internal element's computed style

results.message: When content-visibility: hidden is not supported, a @supports not (content-visibility: hidden) fallback rule applies display: none to inactive view elements
Inactive view elements have content-visibility: hidden applied in their computed styles
When a view element is active, it does not have content-visibility: hidden applied (its computed content-visibility is visible)
Switching between views toggles the content-visibility state between the active and inactive view elements

results.message: During a forward transition, the ::view-transition-old(root) element has an animation that translates it to -100% on the X-axis
During a forward transition, the ::view-transition-new(root) element has an animation that translates it from 100% on the X-axis
During a backward transition, the ::view-transition-old(root) element has an animation that translates it to 100% on the X-axis

    - region "Sourcing Where do you source your coffee beans?":
      - paragraph: We partner directly with small-scale, sustainable family farms in Colombia, Ethiopia, Guatemala, and Sumatra. Through our Direct Trade relationships, we ensure farmers receive at least 25% above Fair Trade minimums while cultivating shade-grown, 100% Arabica beans harvested at peak ripeness.
    - button "Sourcing Are your coffees certified organic and ethically traded?"
    - region "Sourcing Are your coffees certified organic and ethically traded?":

    - button "Roasting What is the difference between your light, medium, and dark roasts?"
